title: Order of Operations: Parentheses and Brackets
seo_title: Grade 5 Order of Operations Worksheets: Parentheses and Brackets (TEKS 5.4E, 5.4F, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.4E describe the meaning of parentheses and brackets in a numeric expression; 5.4F simplify numerical expressions that do not involve exponents, including up to two levels of grouping
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 order of operations worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.4E and 5.4F: multiply before adding, parentheses, brackets, writing expressions from words and interpreting expressions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Parentheses and brackets first, then × and ÷, then + and −.
key_sub: Work from the innermost grouping out. Multiply and divide from left to right before adding and subtracting.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Do what is inside parentheses ( ) first. With brackets [ ], start with the innermost grouping and work out.
  • Then multiply and divide from left to right.
  • Then add and subtract from left to right.

Examples

Example

[2 + (4 × 5)] × 6

4 × 5 = 20

2 + 20 = 22

22 × 6 = 132

Answer: 132

Example

9 + 5 × 8

5 × 8 = 40

9 + 40 = 49

Answer: 49

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Working left to right: 9 + 5 × 8 = 112Multiply before adding.
Ignoring the inner parentheses in bracketsStart with the innermost grouping.
Putting parentheses in the wrong placeGroup the part that the words say to do first.

faq.a: Describe the meaning of parentheses and brackets in a numeric expression.
Simplify numerical expressions that do not involve exponents, including up to two levels of grouping.

faq.q: What is the difference between parentheses and brackets?
faq.a: Both group numbers. Brackets [ ] are used outside parentheses so you can see the order: [3 × (2 + 5)].

faq.q: Why do we need an order of operations?
faq.a: So everyone gets the same value for the same expression.

sets.title: Multiply and divide before adding and subtracting

items.e: 5 + 6 × 8 = 5 + 48 = 53. Not 88: that comes from working strictly left to right.
48 − 4 × 3 = 48 − 12 = 36. Not 132: that comes from working strictly left to right.
8 × 3 + 4 × 5 = 24 + 4 × 5 = 24 + 20 = 44. Not 140: that comes from working strictly left to right.
12 + 36 ÷ 4 = 12 + 9 = 21. Not 12: that comes from working strictly left to right.
72 ÷ 4 × 2 = 18 × 2 = 36. Not 9: that comes from multiplying before dividing.
108 ÷ 3 × 2 = 36 × 2 = 72. Not 18: that comes from multiplying before dividing.
39 − 8 + 5 = 31 + 5 = 36. Not 26: that comes from adding before subtracting.
62 − 21 + 9 = 41 + 9 = 50. Not 32: that comes from adding before subtracting.
4 × 9 − 6 ÷ 3 = 36 − 6 ÷ 3 = 36 − 2 = 34. Not 10: that comes from working strictly left to right.
24 − 12 ÷ 4 + 6 = 24 − 3 + 6 = 21 + 6 = 27. Not 9: that comes from working strictly left to right.
47 − 13 + 15 − 8 = 34 + 15 − 8 = 49 − 8 = 41. Not 11: that comes from adding before subtracting.
84 − 36 ÷ 6 × 2 = 84 − 6 × 2 = 84 − 12 = 72. Not 81: that comes from multiplying before dividing.
11 + 5 × 9 − 7 = 11 + 45 − 7 = 56 − 7 = 49. Not 137: that comes from working strictly left to right.
4 × 310 − 38 + 13 = 1,240 − 38 + 13 = 1,202 + 13 = 1,215. Not 1,189: that comes from adding before subtracting.

items.q: Which part of 18 − 6 ÷ 3 + 2 do you work out first?
items.e: Divide first because ÷ comes before + and −: 18 − 2 + 2. Then go left to right: 16 + 2 = 18.

items.q: Which part of 40 − 8 + 2 × 5 do you work out first?
items.e: Multiply first: 40 − 8 + 10. Then go left to right: 32 + 10 = 42.

items.q: Which part of 30 ÷ 5 × 2 + 4 do you work out first?
items.e: × and ÷ are on the same level, so go left to right: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 first. Then 6 × 2 = 12, and 12 + 4 = 16.
24 ÷ 4 × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12. Ximena multiplied before dividing, but × and ÷ go from left to right.
6 + 4 × 5 = 6 + 20 = 26. Josiah added first, but you multiply before you add.
20 − 6 + 4 = 14 + 4 = 18. Jayden added before subtracting, but + and − go from left to right.
8 × (6 + 4) = 8 × 10 = 80. Not 52: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(9 + 3) × 5 = 12 × 5 = 60. Not 24: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(16 − 3) × 4 = 13 × 4 = 52. Not 4: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
4 × (17 − 2) = 4 × 15 = 60. Not 66: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(42 + 18) ÷ 6 = 60 ÷ 6 = 10. Not 45: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
72 ÷ (12 − 4) = 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Not 2: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
52 − (12 + 8) = 52 − 20 = 32. Not 48: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
40 − (23 − 9) = 40 − 14 = 26. Not 8: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(8 + 2) × (10 − 6) = 10 × (10 − 6) = 10 × 4 = 40. Not 22: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(33 − 12) ÷ (2 + 1) = 21 ÷ (2 + 1) = 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Not 28: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
4 × (1,300 + 200) = 4 × 1,500 = 6,000. Not 5,400: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(1,200 − 160) ÷ 8 = 1,040 ÷ 8 = 130. Not 1,180: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
5 + 6 × (15 − 2) = 5 + 6 × 13 = 5 + 78 = 83. Not 93: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(4 + 8) × 6 − 5 = 12 × 6 − 5 = 72 − 5 = 67. Not 47: that comes from skipping the parentheses.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 30?
items.e: 2 × (8 + 7) = 2 × 15 = 30. Without the parentheses, 2 × 8 + 7 = 23, because you multiply before you add.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 48?
items.e: 4 × (9 + 3) = 4 × 12 = 48. Without the parentheses, 4 × 9 + 3 = 39, because you multiply before you add.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 84?
items.e: 6 × (10 + 4) = 6 × 14 = 84. Without the parentheses, 6 × 10 + 4 = 64, because you multiply before you add.
(12 + 5) × 3 = 17 × 3 = 51. Without the parentheses the value changes: 12 + 5 × 3 = 27.

items.q: Which expression has the same value as 6 + (4 × 5)?
items.e: 6 + (4 × 5) = 6 + 20 = 26. 6 + 4 × 5 is also 26, because you multiply first anyway. (6 + 4) × 5 = 50 is different.
9 × (8 + 6) = 9 × 14 = 126. Not 78: that comes from skipping the parentheses.

sets.title: Brackets: work from the inside out

items.e: [8 + (5 × 4)] × 3 = [8 + 20] × 3 = 28 × 3 = 84. Work from the inside out. Not 68: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
{70 − [2 × (4 + 1)]} = {70 − [2 × 5]} = {70 − 10} = 60. Work from the inside out. Not 63: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
3 × [25 − (12 − 2)] = 3 × [25 − 10] = 3 × 15 = 45. Work from the inside out. Not 33: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[(24 + 12) ÷ 4] × 2 = [36 ÷ 4] × 2 = 9 × 2 = 18. Work from the inside out. Not 54: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
13 + [4 × (14 − 7)] = 13 + [4 × 7] = 13 + 28 = 41. Work from the inside out. Not 62: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
{[5 × (11 − 3)] + 6} ÷ 2 = {[5 × 8] + 6} ÷ 2 = {40 + 6} ÷ 2 = 46 ÷ 2 = 23. Work from the inside out. Not 29: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[29 − (8 + 5)] × 4 = [29 − 13] × 4 = 16 × 4 = 64. Work from the inside out. Not 104: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
71 − [(4 + 6) × 5] = 71 − [10 × 5] = 71 − 50 = 21. Work from the inside out. Not 37: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
3 × {5 + [38 − (4 × 2)]} = 3 × {5 + [38 − 8]} = 3 × {5 + 30} = 3 × 35 = 105. Work from the inside out. Not 45: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
[1,500 − (25 × 8)] ÷ 4 = [1,500 − 200] ÷ 4 = 1,300 ÷ 4 = 325. Work from the inside out. Not 1,450: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
{144 ÷ [2 × (7 − 5)]} + 4 = {144 ÷ [2 × 2]} + 4 = {144 ÷ 4} + 4 = 36 + 4 = 40. Work from the inside out. Not 503: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[4 × (9 + 2)] − [3 × (7 − 5)] = [4 × 11] − [3 × (7 − 5)] = 44 − [3 × (7 − 5)] = 44 − [3 × 2] = 44 − 6 = 38. Work from the inside out. Not 22: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
50 × [70 − (20 + 12)] = 50 × [70 − 32] = 50 × 38 = 1,900. Work from the inside out. Not 3,100: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
{[(4 + 3) × 6] − 8} ÷ 2 = {[7 × 6] − 8} ÷ 2 = {42 − 8} ÷ 2 = 34 ÷ 2 = 17. Work from the inside out. Not 7: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.

items.q: Which part of {20 − [2 × (3 + 1)]} do you work out first?
items.e: Start with the innermost grouping symbols, the parentheses: 3 + 1. Then work outward: {20 − [2 × (3 + 1)]} = {20 − [2 × 4]} = {20 − 8} = 12.

items.q: Which part of [30 − (4 × 5)] ÷ 2 do you work out first?
items.e: Start with the innermost grouping symbols, the parentheses: 4 × 5. Then work outward: [30 − (4 × 5)] ÷ 2 = [30 − 20] ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

items.q: Which part of 6 × [10 − (2 + 5)] do you work out first?
items.e: Start with the innermost grouping symbols, the parentheses: 2 + 5. Then work outward: 6 × [10 − (2 + 5)] = 6 × [10 − 7] = 6 × 3 = 18.
[3 + (4 × 2)] × 5 = [3 + 8] × 5 = 11 × 5 = 55. Gabriel skipped the grouping symbols and multiplied first.
{30 − [3 × (2 + 4)]} = {30 − [3 × 6]} = {30 − 18} = 12. Josiah skipped the parentheses inside the brackets.
[(12 + 6) ÷ 3] × 2 = [18 ÷ 3] × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12. Isabella skipped the parentheses and divided 6 ÷ 3 first.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2.
items.e: Add first, so 8 + 7 goes in parentheses. Then multiply by 2: 2 × (8 + 7) = 30. 2 × 8 + 7 would multiply first.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Subtract 5 from the product of 6 and 9.
items.e: “The product of 6 and 9” is 6 × 9. “Subtract 5 from” it means take 5 away from it: 6 × 9 − 5 = 49. 5 − 6 × 9 has the order backward.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Multiply 4 by the sum of 12 and 3.
items.e: “The sum of 12 and 3” is 12 + 3, and it must be found first, so it goes in parentheses: 4 × (12 + 3) = 60.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Divide the difference of 30 and 6 by 4.
items.e: “The difference of 30 and 6” is 30 − 6. Put it in parentheses so you subtract first, then divide by 4: (30 − 6) ÷ 4 = 6.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Add 9 to the quotient of 40 and 5.
items.e: “The quotient of 40 and 5” is 40 ÷ 5. Add 9 to it: 40 ÷ 5 + 9 = 8 + 9 = 17. No parentheses are needed, because ÷ comes first anyway.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Three times the sum of 15 and 6
items.e: “Three times” something means 3 × that amount. The amount is the sum 15 + 6, so it goes in parentheses: 3 × (15 + 6) = 63.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Subtract 8 from 50, then divide by 6.
items.e: “Subtract 8 from 50” is 50 − 8, not 8 − 50. It comes first, so it goes in parentheses: (50 − 8) ÷ 6 = 42 ÷ 6 = 7.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
The product of 7 and the difference of 20 and 4
items.e: “The difference of 20 and 4” is 20 − 4. Multiply it by 7, so it needs parentheses: 7 × (20 − 4) = 7 × 16 = 112.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Add the product of 3 and 8 to the product of 5 and 2.
items.e: Each product is a multiplication: 3 × 8 and 5 × 2. Then add them: 3 × 8 + 5 × 2 = 24 + 10 = 34.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Divide 36 by 4, then subtract the result from 20.
items.e: 36 ÷ 4 is the result. “Subtract the result from 20” means 20 − (36 ÷ 4). Division comes first anyway: 20 − 36 ÷ 4 = 20 − 9 = 11.
The parentheses are worked first: 9 − 2, which is “subtract 2 from 9.” Then the result is multiplied by 4.

c: Divide 3 by the sum of 18 and 6
items.e: The parentheses come first: add 18 and 6. Then divide that sum by 3. (18 + 6) ÷ 3 = 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

c: Subtract 20 from the product of 3 and 4
Subtract the product of 3 and 4 from 20
items.e: Multiplication comes first, so 3 × 4 is found first. Then it is taken away from 20: 20 − 12 = 8.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
6 + 4 × 9 − 12 = 78

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
12 − 2 × 3 + 4 = 34

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
5 × 9 + 6 × 2 = 150

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
12 + 10 ÷ 2 × 3 = 33

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
12 − 3 + 2 × 4 = 44

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
10 × 4 − 6 ÷ 2 = 17

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
10 + 4 × 3 + 2 = 44
Without calculating, how does 3 × (18,932 + 921) compare with 18,932 + 921?
items.e: 3 × (18,932 + 921) is 3 groups of the sum 18,932 + 921, so it is 3 times as large. Adding 3 would make it only 3 more.

items.q: Without calculating, how does (4,520 − 386) ÷ 2 compare with 4,520 − 386?
items.e: Dividing by 2 splits the difference 4,520 − 386 into 2 equal parts, so the value is half as large.

items.q: Without calculating, how does 10 × (73 + 1,409) compare with 73 + 1,409?
items.e: 10 × (73 + 1,409) is 10 groups of the sum 73 + 1,409, so it is 10 times as large.

items.q: Which expression is twice as large as 645 + 317?
items.e: Twice as large means 2 groups of the whole sum, so the sum goes in parentheses: 2 × (645 + 317). 2 × 645 + 317 doubles only 645.

items.q: Which expression is 4 times as large as 9 × 1,206?
items.e: Multiplying 9 × 1,206 by 4 makes it 4 times as large: 4 × 9 × 1,206. Adding 4 makes it only 4 more.
Both use the same sum, 2,346 + 78. 5 groups of it are more than 4 groups, so 5 × (2,346 + 78) is greater.

items.q: Without calculating, how does 8 × 395 + 8 compare with 8 × 395?
items.e: 8 × 395 + 8 is 8 × 395 with 8 added, so it is 8 more. The + 8 is not multiplied, because there are no parentheses.

items.q: Jayden says 6 × (250 + 39) is 6 more than 250 + 39. Is he right?
c: No, it is 39 times as large
No, it is 6 times as large
items.e: 6 × (250 + 39) is 6 groups of 250 + 39, so it is 6 times as large. It would be 6 more only if it were 250 + 39 + 6.

items.q: Emma buys 3 packs of 12 pencils and 5 extra pencils. Which expression shows how many pencils she buys?
items.e: 3 packs of 12 is 3 × 12. The 5 extra pencils are added once, not to every pack: 3 × 12 + 5 = 36 + 5 = 41.

items.q: Carlos has $50. He buys 4 books that cost $9 each. Which expression shows how much money he has left?
items.e: The books cost 4 × 9. Take that away from 50: 50 − 4 × 9 = 50 − 36 = 14. Multiplication comes first, so no parentheses are needed.

items.q: 28 students and 4 teachers split into 2 equal groups for a field trip. Which expression shows how many people are in each group?
items.e: First find everyone: 28 + 4. Then split into 2 groups. The sum must be found first, so it goes in parentheses: (28 + 4) ÷ 2 = 16.

items.q: Each of 6 tables has 4 red cups and 5 blue cups. Which expression shows how many cups there are in all?
items.e: Each table has 4 + 5 cups, and there are 6 tables: 6 × (4 + 5) = 6 × 9 = 54. 6 × 4 + 5 forgets the blue cups on 5 of the tables.

items.q: Josiah saves $12 a week for 5 weeks. Then he spends $18. Which expression shows how much money he has now?
items.e: Josiah saves 12 × 5 dollars. Then $18 is taken away: 12 × 5 − 18 = 60 − 18 = 42. 18 − 12 × 5 has the order backward.

items.q: Diego had 120 stickers. He gave 15 stickers to each of 4 friends. Which expression shows how many stickers he has left?
items.e: Diego gave away 4 × 15 stickers. Take that from 120: 120 − 4 × 15 = 120 − 60 = 60.

items.q: A movie ticket costs $9 and a bag of popcorn costs $5. A family of 4 gets a ticket and a bag of popcorn for each person. They pay with a $100 bill. How much change do they get?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: 100 − 4 × (9 + 5) = 100 − 4 × 14 = 100 − 56 = 44. Not $69: that skips the parentheses. Not $56: that is the cost, not the change. Answer: $44.

items.q: A school orders 12 boxes of 24 markers. 30 markers are broken. The rest are shared equally by 6 classes. How many markers does each class get?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: (12 × 24 − 30) ÷ 6 = (288 − 30) ÷ 6 = 258 ÷ 6 = 43. The subtraction must come before the division, so it goes in parentheses. Not 283: that divides before subtracting. Answer: 43 markers.

items.q: A bakery makes 8 trays of 15 muffins and 4 trays of 12 muffins. At the end of the day, 20 muffins are left. How many muffins did the bakery sell?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: 8 × 15 + 4 × 12 − 20 = 120 + 4 × 12 − 20 = 120 + 48 − 20 = 168 − 20 = 148. Find both products first and add them, then subtract the 20 muffins that were left. 168 is all the muffins, not the ones sold. Answer: 148 muffins.

items.q: A class trip costs $1,250 for each adult and $875 for each child. How much do 3 adults and 2 children pay in all?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: 3 × 1,250 + 2 × 875 = 3,750 + 2 × 875 = 3,750 + 1,750 = 5,500. Multiply each price by the number of people first, then add. Not $4,625: that counts only 1 child. Answer: $5,500.

items.q: Caleb says 6 × (250 + 39) is 6 more than 250 + 39. Is he right?
c: No, it is 39 times as large
No, it is 6 times as large
items.e: 6 × (250 + 39) is 6 groups of 250 + 39, so it is 6 times as large. It would be 6 more only if it were 250 + 39 + 6.

items.q: Carlos buys 3 packs of 12 pencils and 5 extra pencils. Which expression shows how many pencils he buys?
items.e: 3 packs of 12 is 3 × 12. The 5 extra pencils are added once, not to every pack: 3 × 12 + 5 = 36 + 5 = 41.
